Question:
Among all the current legislators who have served for more than 4 terms, what is the percentage of them being female?

Evidence:
have served for more than 4 years refers to count(bioguide) > 4; percentage = MULTIPLY(DIVIDE(SUM(gender_bio = 'F'), count(bioguide)), 100.0); female refers to gender_bio = 'F'
answer: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN gender_bio = 'F' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T3.bioguide) FROM ( SELECT T2.bioguide, T1.gender_bio FROM current AS T1 INNER JOIN `current-terms` AS T2 ON T1.bioguide_id = T2.bioguide GROUP BY T2.bioguide HAVING COUNT(T2.bioguide) > 4 ) T3

Question:
How many employees sold over 20,000 quantities of "Touring-2000 Blue, 50"?

Evidence:
over 20,000 quantities refers to Quantity > 20000; 'Touring-2000 Blue, 50' is name of product;

Question:
On how many days with the max temperature over 90 did the sale of item no.5 in store no.3 exceed 100?

Evidence:
max temperature over 90 refers to tmax > 90; item no. 5 refers to item_nbr = 5; store no.3 refers to store_nbr = 3; sale exceed 100 refers to units > 100; number of days refers to count (date)
answer: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN units > 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count FROM sales_in_weather AS T1 INNER JOIN relation AS T2 ON T1.store_nbr = T2.store_nbr INNER JOIN weather AS T3 ON T2.station_nbr = T3.station_nbr WHERE T2.store_nbr = 3 AND SUBSTR(T1.`date`, 1, 4) = '2012' AND T1.item_nbr = 5 AND tmax > 90

Question:
List the long name of teams with above-average build-up play passing in 2012.

Evidence:
long name of teams refers to team_long_name; build-up play passing refers to buildUpPlayPassing; above-average build-up play passing = buildUpPlayPassing > DIVIDE(SUM(buildUpPlayPassing), COUNT(team_long_name) WHERE buildUpPlayPassing IS NOT NULL); in 2012 refers to strftime('%Y', date) = '2012';
answer: SELECT DISTINCT t4.team_long_name FROM Team_Attributes AS t3 INNER JOIN Team AS t4 ON t3.team_api_id = t4.team_api_id WHERE SUBSTR(t3.`date`, 1, 4) = '2012' AND t3.buildUpPlayPassing > ( SELECT CAST(SUM(t2.buildUpPlayPassing) AS REAL) / COUNT(t1.id) FROM Team AS t1 INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS t2 ON t1.team_api_id = t2.team_api_id WHERE STRFTIME('%Y',t2.`date`) = '2012')

Question:
How many people were there in the Engineering Department in the year 2009?

Evidence:
year(EndDate)>2009 and year(StartDate)<2009;
answer: SELECT COUNT(T1.BusinessEntityID) FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Department AS T3 ON T2.DepartmentID = T3.DepartmentID WHERE T3.Name = 'Engineering' AND STRFTIME('%Y', T2.EndDate) > '2009' AND STRFTIME('%Y', T2.StartDate) < '2009'

answer: SELECT DISTINCT T1.ID FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T1.Admission = '-' AND T2.`T-BIL` < 2.0 AND T2.Date LIKE '1991-10-%'

Question:
How much is the average salary of female employees in comparison to male employees?

Evidence:
female refers to Gender = 'F'; male refers to Gender = 'M'; difference in the average salary of female against male employees = SUBTRACT(AVG(Rate where Gender = 'F')), (AVG(Rate where Gender = 'M')));
answer: SELECT AVG(T2.Rate) FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeePayHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.Gender = 'F'

prefix_hints.hint_2: I project the member name and hometown from the joined member records This completes the query: `SELECT T2.name ,  T2.hometown FROM membership_register_branch AS T1 JOIN member AS T2 ON T1.member_id  =  T2.member_id WHERE T1.register_year  =  2016`.

Question:
What is the percentage of the customers who used EUR in 2012/8/25?

Evidence:
'2012/8/25' can be represented by '2012-08-25'
answer: SELECT CAST(SUM(IIF(T2.Currency = 'EUR', 1, 0)) AS FLOAT) * 100 / COUNT(T1.CustomerID) FROM transactions_1k AS T1 INNER JOIN customers AS T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID WHERE T1.Date = '2012-08-25'

prefix_hints.hint_1: The dated activity comes from `transactions_1k`, so I begin with that transaction source I link each transaction to its customer so the customer's currency is available I restrict the transactions to the given date represented as `2012-08-25`: `FROM transactions_1k AS T1 INNER JOIN customers AS T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID WHERE T1.Date = '2012-08-25'`.

Question:
List all outpatient within normal range of creatinine phosphokinase. Give me the distinct ids.

Evidence:
outpatient refers to Admission = '-'; normal range of creatinine phosphokinase refers to CPK < 250;
answer: SELECT DISTINCT T1.ID FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.CPK < 250 AND T1.Admission = '-'

metadata.question: List all outpatient within normal range of creatinine phosphokinase. Give me the distinct ids.
metadata.evidence: outpatient refers to Admission = '-'; normal range of creatinine phosphokinase refers to CPK < 250;

prefix_hints.hint_1: Patient admission status is in `Patient`, while creatinine phosphokinase values are in `Laboratory`, so I start from both tables I link each laboratory record to its patient by the shared ID I keep laboratory records whose CPK value is within the stated normal range below 250: `FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.CPK < 250`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I further restrict the patients to outpatients, represented by an admission value of `-` I return distinct patient IDs because a patient can have multiple qualifying laboratory records: `SELECT DISTINCT T1.ID FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.CPK < 250 AND T1.Admission = '-'`.

Question:
In California, how many delivery receptacles are there in the community post office that has the highest number of delivery receptacles?

Evidence:
in California refers to name = 'California' and state = 'CA'; 'Community Post Office' is the Type
answer: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM state AS T1 INNER JOIN zip_data AS T2 ON T1.abbreviation = T2.state WHERE T1.abbreviation = 'CA' AND T2.type LIKE '%Community Post Office%' AND T1.name = 'California' AND T2.state = 'CA'

Question:
Please list the names of the products that get over 10 reviews and a salable.

Evidence:
salable product refers to FinishedGoodsFlag = 1; over 10 reviews refers to count(comments)>10
answer: SELECT T2.NAME FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.FinishedGoodsFlag = 1 GROUP BY T2.NAME ORDER BY COUNT(T1.comments) > 10

Question:
Name the card and artist with the most ruling information. Also state if the card is a promotional printing.

Evidence:
with the most ruling information refers to Max(count(rulings.uuid)); the card is the promotional printing refers to isPromo = 1;
answer: SELECT T1.name, T1.artist, T1.isPromo FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN rulings AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.isPromo = 1 AND T1.artist = (SELECT artist FROM cards WHERE isPromo = 1 GROUP BY artist HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT uuid) = (SELECT MAX(count_uuid) FROM ( SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT uuid) AS count_uuid FROM cards WHERE isPromo = 1 GROUP BY artist ))) LIMIT 1

league with highest matches of all time refers to MAX(COUNT(league_id));

Question:
Among the employees in the Manufacturing group in 2007, how many of them are store contacts?

Evidence:
store contact refers to PersonType = 'SC'; year(EndDate)>2007 and year(StartDate)<2007;
answer: SELECT COUNT(T1.BusinessEntityID) FROM EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T1 INNER JOIN Department AS T2 ON T1.DepartmentID = T2.DepartmentID INNER JOIN Person AS T3 ON T1.BusinessEntityID WHERE T3.PersonType = 'SC' AND T2.GroupName = 'Manufacturing' AND STRFTIME('%Y', T1.EndDate) >= '2007' AND STRFTIME('%Y', T1.StartDate) <= '2007'

Question:
Among universities that score below 80 in 2015, what is the percentage of international students?

Evidence:
score below 80 refers to score < 80; in 2015 refers to year 2015; percentage of international students refers to DIVIDE(SUM(DIVIDE(MULTIPLY(num_students, pct_international_students), 100)), SUM(num_students))
answer: SELECT SUM(CAST(T1.num_students * T1.pct_international_students AS REAL) / 100) / COUNT(*) * 100 FROM university_year AS T1 INNER JOIN university_ranking_year AS T2 ON T1.university_id = T2.university_id WHERE T2.score < 80 AND T1.year = 2015

How many times did the matches were held in MA Chidambaram Stadium from 5/9/2009 to 8/8/2011?

Question:

Evidence:
Hematoclit is normal refers to 29 < N < 52; highest anti-Cardiolipin antibody concentration refers to MAX(`aCL IgA`);
answer: SELECT DISTINCT T1.ID FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Examination AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T3 on T1.ID = T3.ID WHERE (T3.HCT >= 52 OR T3.HCT <= 29) ORDER BY T2.`aCL IgA` DESC LIMIT 1

answer: SELECT t3.house_number  ,  t1.name FROM restaurant AS t1 JOIN geographic AS t2 ON t1.city_name  =  t2.city_name JOIN LOCATION AS t3 ON t1.id  =  t3.restaurant_id WHERE t2.region  =  "bay area" AND t1.food_type  =  "american" AND t1.rating  =  ( SELECT MAX ( t1.rating ) FROM restaurant AS t1 JOIN geographic AS t2 ON t1.city_name  =  t2.city_name WHERE t2.region  =  "bay area" AND t1.food_type  =  "american" );

metadata.question: what is the best american restaurant in the bay area ?

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start with restaurants and join their cities to the geographic data so I can identify the Bay Area I also join each restaurant to its location so the house number is available in the result I restrict the candidates to American restaurants in the Bay Area: `FROM restaurant AS t1 JOIN geographic AS t2 ON t1.city_name = t2.city_name JOIN LOCATION AS t3 ON t1.id = t3.restaurant_id WHERE t2.region = "bay area" AND t1.food_type = "american"`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I identify the best candidate by requiring its rating to equal the maximum rating among American restaurants in the same region Finally, I return the house number and restaurant name for every restaurant tied at that maximum rating: `SELECT t3.house_number  ,  t1.name FROM restaurant AS t1 JOIN geographic AS t2 ON t1.city_name  =  t2.city_name JOIN LOCATION AS t3 ON t1.id  =  t3.restaurant_id WHERE t2.region  =  "bay area" AND t1.food_type  =  "american" AND t1.rating  =  ( SELECT MAX ( t1.rating ) FROM restaurant AS t1 JOIN geographic AS t2 ON t1.city_name  =  t2.city_name WHERE t2.region  =  "bay area" AND t1.food_type  =  "american" );`.

Question:
Among the employees who are married and wish to receive e-mail promotions, how much higher is their highest pay rate from the average pay rate?

Evidence:
married refers to MaritalStatus = 'M'; Contact does wish to receive e-mail promotions from Adventure Works refers to EmailPromotion = 1; Average = Divide (Sum(Rate (MaritalStatus = 'M' & EmailPromotion = 1))), Count (BusinessEntityID (MaritalStatus = 'M' & EmailPromotion = 1)); MAX(Rate (MaritalStatus = 'M' & EmailPromotion = 1) - Average;
answer: SELECT MAX(T1.Rate) - SUM(T1.Rate) / COUNT(T1.BusinessEntityID) FROM EmployeePayHistory AS T1 INNER JOIN Person AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Employee AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID WHERE T2.EmailPromotion = 2 AND T3.MaritalStatus = 'M'

Question:
What is the name of organization that has the greatest number of contact individuals?
answer: SELECT t1.organization_name FROM organizations AS t1 JOIN organization_contact_individuals AS t2 ON t1.organization_id  =  t2.organization_id GROUP BY t1.organization_name ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1

metadata.question: What is the name of organization that has the greatest number of contact individuals?

prefix_hints.hint_1: I link each organization to its contact-individual records through the shared organization id I group the joined records by organization name so each group represents one organization's contacts I order the organization groups by their contact-record counts in descending order, placing the greatest count first: `FROM organizations AS t1 JOIN organization_contact_individuals AS t2 ON t1.organization_id  =  t2.organization_id GROUP BY t1.organization_name ORDER BY count(*) DESC`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I keep only the first group to identify the organization with the greatest number of contact individuals Finally, I return that organization's name: `SELECT t1.organization_name FROM organizations AS t1 JOIN organization_contact_individuals AS t2 ON t1.organization_id  =  t2.organization_id GROUP BY t1.organization_name ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:

answer: SELECT DISTINCT T1.category_name FROM Categories AS T1 INNER JOIN Business_Categories AS T2 ON T1.category_id = T2.category_id INNER JOIN Business AS T3 ON T2.business_id = T3.business_id INNER JOIN Tips AS T4 ON T3.business_id = T4.business_id WHERE T4.tip_length LIKE 'short'

Question:
Provide the names of the products with a profit greater than 98% of the average profit of all products in the East region.

Evidence:
names of the products refers to "Product Name";  profit greater than 98% of the average profit refers to Profit > MULTIPLY(AVG(Profit), 0.98)
answer: SELECT DISTINCT T2.`Product Name` FROM east_superstore AS T1 INNER JOIN product AS T2 ON T1.`Product ID` = T2.`Product ID` WHERE T2.Region = 'East' AND T1.Profit > ( SELECT AVG(Profit) * 0.98 FROM east_superstore )

intermediate_turns.sql: Select T1.Maker, T2.CountryName from Car_Makers as T1 JOIN Countries as T2 on T1.Country = T2.CountryId;

intermediate_turns.question: Also provide the continent name for each!
intermediate_turns.sql: SELECT T1.Continent,  T3.Maker, T2.CountryName FROM CONTINENTS AS T1 JOIN COUNTRIES AS T2 ON T1.ContId  =  T2.continent JOIN car_makers AS T3 ON T2.CountryId  =  T3.Country;

intermediate_turns.question: How many car makers are there per continent?
intermediate_turns.sql: SELECT T1.Continent ,  count(*) FROM CONTINENTS AS T1 JOIN COUNTRIES AS T2 ON T1.ContId  =  T2.continent JOIN car_makers AS T3 ON T2.CountryId  =  T3.Country GROUP BY T1.Continent;

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start from continents and connect each one to its countries through the continent identifier I then join each country to its car makers using the country identifier I group the joined maker rows by continent name so each continent can have its own count: `FROM CONTINENTS AS T1 JOIN COUNTRIES AS T2 ON T1.ContId  =  T2.continent JOIN car_makers AS T3 ON T2.CountryId  =  T3.Country GROUP BY T1.Continent`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I project the continent name and count all maker rows in each group This completes the continent-level maker count: `SELECT T1.Continent ,  count(*) FROM CONTINENTS AS T1 JOIN COUNTRIES AS T2 ON T1.ContId  =  T2.continent JOIN car_makers AS T3 ON T2.CountryId  =  T3.Country GROUP BY T1.Continent;`.

Question:
Provide the ingredients that are rationed in the recipe with the highest carbohydrate content.

Evidence:
the highest carbohydrate content refers to MAX(carbo)
answer: SELECT T1.name FROM Ingredient AS T1 INNER JOIN Quantity AS T2 ON T1.ingredient_id = T2.ingredient_id INNER JOIN Nutrition AS T3 ON T3.recipe_id = T2.recipe_id WHERE T2.max_qty = T2.min_qty ORDER BY T3.carbo DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start with ingredients and connect each one to its recipe quantity record through the ingredient id I join the nutrition data on the recipe id so the carbohydrate content is available for each matched ingredient I keep rationed ingredients by requiring their maximum and minimum quantities to be equal: `FROM Ingredient AS T1 INNER JOIN Quantity AS T2 ON T1.ingredient_id = T2.ingredient_id INNER JOIN Nutrition AS T3 ON T3.recipe_id = T2.recipe_id WHERE T2.max_qty = T2.min_qty`.

metadata.question: Find the checking balance of the accounts whose savings balance is higher than the average savings balance.

intermediate_turns.question: What is the average savings balance?
intermediate_turns.sql: SELECT avg(balance) FROM savings

intermediate_turns.question: How many people have savings account balances over it?
intermediate_turns.sql: SELECT count(*)  FROM savings where balance > (SELECT avg(balance) FROM savings)

intermediate_turns.question: What are their names?
intermediate_turns.sql: SELECT T1.name FROM accounts AS T1 JOIN savings AS T2 ON T1.custid  =  T2.custid WHERE T2.balance  >  (SELECT avg(balance) FROM savings)

intermediate_turns.question: What are their checking account balances?
intermediate_turns.sql: SELECT T2.balance FROM accounts AS T1 JOIN checking AS T2 ON T1.custid  =  T2.custid WHERE T1.name IN (SELECT T1.name FROM accounts AS T1 JOIN savings AS T2 ON T1.custid  =  T2.custid WHERE T2.balance  >  (SELECT avg(balance) FROM savings))

prefix_hints.hint_1: I first calculate the average savings balance as the threshold I join accounts to savings and select the names whose savings balance exceeds that threshold I join accounts to checking, then retain accounts whose names appear in the qualifying savings-account query: `FROM accounts AS T1 JOIN checking AS T2 ON T1.custid  =  T2.custid WHERE T1.name IN (SELECT T1.name FROM accounts AS T1 JOIN savings AS T2 ON T1.custid  =  T2.custid WHERE T2.balance  >  (SELECT avg(balance) FROM savings))`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I project the checking balance for each matched account This completes the query: `SELECT T2.balance FROM accounts AS T1 JOIN checking AS T2 ON T1.custid  =  T2.custid WHERE T1.name IN (SELECT T1.name FROM accounts AS T1 JOIN savings AS T2 ON T1.custid  =  T2.custid WHERE T2.balance  >  (SELECT avg(balance) FROM savings))`.

prefix_hints.hint_1: I link each gymnast to their personal record so the hometown is available I group the matched gymnasts by hometown so each town forms one group I sort the hometown groups by their gymnast counts in descending order, placing the most common first: `FROM gymnast AS T1 JOIN people AS T2 ON T1.Gymnast_ID  =  T2.People_ID GROUP BY T2.Hometown ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I keep only the first group after that ranking I project the hometown from the highest-count group, completing the query: `SELECT T2.Hometown FROM gymnast AS T1 JOIN people AS T2 ON T1.Gymnast_ID  =  T2.People_ID GROUP BY T2.Hometown ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1`.

At what latitude is the Thomas Kemper brand beer consumed the most?

Question:
In which city has the greatest population, what is its percentage to its country population?
answer: SELECT T3.Name, CAST(T3.Population AS REAL) * 100 / T1.Population FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN province AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN city AS T3 ON T3.Country = T2.Country ORDER BY T3.Population DESC LIMIT 1

metadata.question: In which city has the greatest population, what is its percentage to its country population?

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start with each country and its provinces, linking the country code to the province country identifier I add the cities by matching their country identifier to the province country identifier I project the city name and calculate its population as a percentage of the country population, casting the city population to REAL for division: `SELECT T3.Name, CAST(T3.Population AS REAL) * 100 / T1.Population FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN province AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN city AS T3 ON T3.Country = T2.Country`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I sort cities by population in descending order so the greatest population appears first I retain the first row to return the city with the greatest population and its percentage of the country population: `SELECT T3.Name, CAST(T3.Population AS REAL) * 100 / T1.Population FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN province AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN city AS T3 ON T3.Country = T2.Country ORDER BY T3.Population DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
Of all the countries in which English is spoken, what percentage has English as their only language?

Evidence:
Percentage = [count(countries 100% English) / count(countries English)] * 100%
answer: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.Percentage = 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.Name) FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN language AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T2.Name = 'English'

Question:
Which year recorded the most number of goals by a player and how old was the player at the time the most number of goals was achieved by him?

Evidence:
most number of goals refers to max(G); how old refers to age = subtract(year(max(G)), birthYear)
answer: SELECT T1.year, T1.year - T2.birthYear FROM Scoring AS T1 INNER JOIN Master AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID GROUP BY T1.year, T1.year - T2.birthYear ORDER BY SUM(T1.G) DESC LIMIT 1

Evidence:
Medline is the name of the customer; DIVIDE(COUNT(OrderNumber where Sales Channel = 'In-Store' and Customer Names = 'Medline'), COUNT(OrderNumber where Customer Names = 'Medline')) as percentage;

Question:
What are the first and last names of all the employees and how many people report to them?
answer: SELECT T2.first_name , T2.last_name ,  count(T1.reports_to) FROM employees AS T1 JOIN employees AS T2 ON T1.reports_to = T2.id GROUP BY T1.reports_to ORDER BY count(T1.reports_to) DESC LIMIT 1;

metadata.question: What are the first and last names of all the employees and how many people report to them?

prefix_hints.hint_1: I self-join `employees` so each employee record in `T1` is linked to the employee in `T2` whom they report to I group by the manager identifier so each group contains all employees reporting to the same person I order the manager groups by their number of reports in descending order: `FROM employees AS T1 JOIN employees AS T2 ON T1.reports_to = T2.id GROUP BY T1.reports_to ORDER BY count(T1.reports_to) DESC`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I keep the first group, which identifies the employee with the most direct reports I project that employee's first and last names together with the report count, completing the query: `SELECT T2.first_name , T2.last_name ,  count(T1.reports_to) FROM employees AS T1 JOIN employees AS T2 ON T1.reports_to = T2.id GROUP BY T1.reports_to ORDER BY count(T1.reports_to) DESC LIMIT 1;`.

answer: SELECT T2.Name FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN city AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T1.Name = ( SELECT Name FROM country ORDER BY CAST(Population AS REAL) / Area LIMIT 11, 1 ) ORDER BY T2.Population DESC LIMIT 1

Question:

Evidence:
longest vacation hour refers to max(VacationHours)
answer: SELECT T1.Rate FROM EmployeePayHistory AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID ORDER BY T2.VacationHours DESC LIMIT 1

Question:
Which department has the most professors with a Ph.D.?
answer: SELECT T2.dept_name ,  T1.dept_code FROM professor AS T1 JOIN department AS T2 ON T1.dept_code  =  T2.dept_code WHERE T1.prof_high_degree  =  'Ph.D.' GROUP BY T1.dept_code ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start with professors and departments, joining them by department code so the department name is available I restrict the joined rows to professors whose highest degree is a Ph.D. I group the qualifying professors by department so each department's rows can be counted: `FROM professor AS T1 JOIN department AS T2 ON T1.dept_code  =  T2.dept_code WHERE T1.prof_high_degree  =  'Ph.D.' GROUP BY T1.dept_code`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I sort the department groups by their professor counts in descending order and retain the largest one I project the winning department's name and code, completing the query: `SELECT T2.dept_name ,  T1.dept_code FROM professor AS T1 JOIN department AS T2 ON T1.dept_code  =  T2.dept_code WHERE T1.prof_high_degree  =  'Ph.D.' GROUP BY T1.dept_code ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
What language was the most used in movies released in 2006?

Evidence:
released in 2006 refers to release_year = 2006; the most used language refers to MAX(COUNT(language_id))
answer: SELECT T.language_id FROM ( SELECT T1.language_id, COUNT(T1.language_id) AS num FROM film AS T1 INNER JOIN language AS T2 ON T1.language_id = T2.language_id WHERE STRFTIME('%Y',T1.release_year) = '2006' GROUP BY T1.language_id ) AS T ORDER BY T.num DESC LIMIT 1

Question:
What is the title and id of the film that has the greatest number of copies in inventory?
answer: SELECT T1.title ,  T1.film_id FROM film AS T1 JOIN inventory AS T2 ON T1.film_id  =  T2.film_id GROUP BY T1.film_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1

metadata.question: What is the title and id of the film that has the greatest number of copies in inventory?

prefix_hints.hint_1: Film titles are in `film`, while each inventory row represents a copy, so I join the two tables by film id I group the joined inventory rows by film so each group represents all copies of one film I order the film groups by their inventory-row counts in descending order, placing the film with the most copies first: `FROM film AS T1 JOIN inventory AS T2 ON T1.film_id  =  T2.film_id GROUP BY T1.film_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I retain only that first, highest-count film group Finally, I return the title and id of the selected film: `SELECT T1.title ,  T1.film_id FROM film AS T1 JOIN inventory AS T2 ON T1.film_id  =  T2.film_id GROUP BY T1.film_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
How many Canadian players, between the ages of 18 and 24 when they initially played their first NHL, had a cumulative goal total of no more than 5? Indicate their complete names, the year, and the team for which they scored the specified amount of goals.

Evidence:
Canadian players mean player whose birthCountry = Canada; ages of 18 and 24 refers to SUBTRACT(firstNHL, birthYear) BETWEEN 18 AND 24; cumulative goal total of no more than 5 refers to G < 5; complete name = nameGiven + lastName
answer: SELECT T2.nameGiven, T2.lastName, T2.birthYear, birthMon, birthDay , T3.tmID FROM Scoring AS T1 INNER JOIN Master AS T2 ON T2.playerID = T1.playerID INNER JOIN Teams AS T3 ON T3.tmID = T1.tmID WHERE (T2.firstNHL - T2.birthYear) BETWEEN 18 AND 24 AND T3.G < 5

How long has the NHL player been playing during the year when he recorded the least number of times being on the ice when a goal is scored for the team versus against the team? Indicate his full name.

Evidence:

Question:
Among the countries with a GDP of over 1000000, how many of them have mountains higher than 1000?
answer: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.Name) FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN geo_mountain AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN economy AS T3 ON T3.Country = T1.Code INNER JOIN mountain AS T4 ON T4.Name = T2.Mountain WHERE T3.GDP > 1000000 AND T4.Height > 1000

Question:
What is the percentage of Swedish players in playoffs games in the 1997 - 2000 season?

Evidence:
percentage = MULTIPLY(DIVIDE(SUM(nation = 'Sweden'), COUNT(ELITEID) WHERE SEASON = '1997-2000'), 100); Swedish refers to nation = 'Sweden'; players refers to PlayerName; playoffs games refers to GAMETYPE = 'Playoffs'; 1997-2000 season refers to 3 consecutive SEASONs : '1997-1998', '1998-1999', '1999-2000';
answer: SELECT DISTINCT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T1.nation = 'Sweden' THEN T1.ELITEID ELSE NULL END) OVER (PARTITION BY T2.SEASON) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.ELITEID) OVER (PARTITION BY T2.SEASON) FROM PlayerInfo AS T1 INNER JOIN SeasonStatus AS T2 ON T1.ELITEID = T2.ELITEID WHERE T2.SEASON IN ('1997-1998', '1998-1999', '1999-2000')

Question:
Please list all the vendors' usual selling prices of the product Hex Nut 5.

Evidence:
vendor's selling price refers to StandardPrice
answer: SELECT T1.StandardPrice FROM ProductVendor AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.Name = 'Hex Nut 5' GROUP BY T1.StandardPrice ORDER BY COUNT(T1.StandardPrice) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: I link vendor pricing to product records through the shared ProductID so I can identify the price for the named product I restrict the joined rows to the product named Hex Nut 5 I group the matching vendor records by StandardPrice so each distinct selling price can be counted: `FROM ProductVendor AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.Name = 'Hex Nut 5' GROUP BY T1.StandardPrice`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I order those price groups by their frequency in descending order and keep the most usual one I project the StandardPrice from the most frequent group, completing the query: `SELECT T1.StandardPrice FROM ProductVendor AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.Name = 'Hex Nut 5' GROUP BY T1.StandardPrice ORDER BY COUNT(T1.StandardPrice) DESC LIMIT 1`.

metadata.question: Please list the full name and region of each employee in alphabetical order.

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start with employees and connect each one to their assigned territories through the employee id I join the territory records so I can follow each assignment toward its region I complete the relationship by joining each territory to its region: `FROM Employees AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeTerritories AS T2 ON T1.EmployeeID = T2.EmployeeID INNER JOIN Territories AS T3 ON T2.TerritoryID = T3.TerritoryID INNER JOIN Region AS T4 ON T3.RegionID = T4.RegionID`.

after retired and became a coach refers to max(subtract(year, lastNHL))

Question:
Among the sales people who achieved projected sales quota 2013, is there any person from territory ID 1? If yes, state the business entity ID.

Evidence:
projected sales quota refers to SalesQuota; projected sales quota in 2013 refers to year(QuotaDate) = 2013;
answer: SELECT DISTINCT T1.BusinessEntityID FROM SalesPerson AS T1 INNER JOIN SalesPersonQuotaHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.TerritoryID = 1 AND STRFTIME('%Y', QuotaDate) = '2013'

prefix_hints.hint_2: I further restrict the matched rows to orders marked with the urgent priority I count the order keys among those qualifying rows to return the requested number: `SELECT COUNT(T2.o_orderkey) FROM lineitem AS T1 INNER JOIN orders AS T2 ON T2.o_orderkey = T1.l_orderkey WHERE JULIANDAY(T1.l_shipdate) - JULIANDAY(T2.o_orderdate) = 1 AND T2.o_orderpriority = '1-URGENT'`.

Question:
From the 'Injured' statuses of the subject, what is the ratio of weapons used are knife against handgun?

Evidence:
the 'Shoot and Miss' status refers to subject_statuses = 'Shoot and Miss'; knife refers to subject_weapon = 'knife'; toy handgun refers to subject_weapon = 'toy handgun'; ratio = divide(count(case_number where subject_weapon = 'knife'), count(case_number where subject_weapon = 'toy handgun')) where subject_statuses = 'Shoot and Miss'
answer: SELECT CAST(SUM(T1.subject_weapon = 'Knife') AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(T1.subject_weapon = 'Handgun') FROM incidents AS T1 INNER JOIN subjects AS T2 ON T1.case_number = T2.case_number WHERE T1.subject_statuses = 'Injured'

prefix_hints.hint_2: I retain customer groups containing more than one policy by checking that their row count exceeds one Finally, I return the details and id of those customers: `SELECT T1.customer_details ,  T1.customer_id FROM Customers AS T1 JOIN Customer_Policies AS T2 ON T1.Customer_id  =  T2.Customer_id GROUP BY T1.customer_id HAVING count(*)  >  1`.

Question:
Among observations in 2011, provide the names and ages of patients whose Systolic Blood Pressures are 200mmHg.

Evidence:
name implies the patient's full name which refers to first, last; age refers to deathdate is null then SUBTRACT(strftime('%Y', DATE), strftime('%Y', birthdate)); Systolic Blood Pressures are 200mmHg refers to DESCRIPTION = 'Systolic Blood Pressure' and VALUE = 200 and UNITS = 'mmHg' from observations; in 2011 refers to DATE like '2011%';
answer: SELECT T2.first, T2.last , CASE WHEN T2.deathdate IS NULL THEN strftime('%Y', T1.DATE) - strftime('%Y', T2.birthdate) ELSE strftime('%Y', T2.deathdate) - strftime('%Y', T2.birthdate) END AS age FROM observations AS T1 INNER JOIN patients AS T2 ON T1.PATIENT = T2.patient WHERE T1.DESCRIPTION = 'Systolic Blood Pressure' AND T1.VALUE = 200 AND T1.UNITS = 'mmHg' AND strftime('%Y', T1.DATE) = '2011'

Question:
Who has the highest average finishing rate between the highest and shortest football player?

Evidence:
finishing rate refers to finishing; highest average finishing rate = MAX(AVG(finishing)); highest football player refers to MAX(height); shortest football player refers to MIN(height);
answer: SELECT A FROM ( SELECT AVG(finishing) result, 'Max' A FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.height = ( SELECT MAX(height) FROM Player ) UNION SELECT AVG(finishing) result, 'Min' A FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.height = ( SELECT MIN(height) FROM Player ) ) ORDER BY result DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_2: I restrict the rows to countries dependent on the United States and to their English-speaking population percentage Finally, I multiply each country's English-language percentage by its total population: `SELECT T2.Percentage * T1.Population FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN language AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN politics AS T3 ON T3.Country = T2.Country WHERE T3.Dependent = 'USA' AND T2.Name = 'English'`.

Question:
What are the ids and names of the battles that led to more than 10 people killed in total.
answer: SELECT T1.id ,  T1.name FROM battle AS T1 JOIN ship AS T2 ON T1.id  =  T2.lost_in_battle JOIN death AS T3 ON T2.id  =  T3.caused_by_ship_id GROUP BY T1.id HAVING sum(T3.killed)  >  10

metadata.question: What are the ids and names of the battles that led to more than 10 people killed in total.

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start from battles and link each one to the ships lost in it through the battle id I then join each ship to the death records it caused so the killed counts are available I group the joined records by battle id so the killed values can be totaled for each battle: `FROM battle AS T1 JOIN ship AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.lost_in_battle JOIN death AS T3 ON T2.id = T3.caused_by_ship_id GROUP BY T1.id`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I retain battle groups whose total number killed is greater than 10 Finally, I return the ids and names of those qualifying battles: `SELECT T1.id ,  T1.name FROM battle AS T1 JOIN ship AS T2 ON T1.id  =  T2.lost_in_battle JOIN death AS T3 ON T2.id  =  T3.caused_by_ship_id GROUP BY T1.id HAVING sum(T3.killed)  >  10`.

Question:
Among the matches in 2013, what is the percentage of winning of the team "Mumbai Indians"?

Evidence:
in 2013 refers to Match_Date like '2013%'; winning of the team "Mumbai Indians" refers to Match_Winner = 7; percentage refers to DIVIDE(COUNT(Match_Winner = 7), COUNT(Match_Winner))
answer: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.Match_Winner = 7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T2.Match_Winner) FROM Team AS T1 INNER JOIN Match AS T2 ON T1.Team_Id = T2.Match_Winner WHERE T2.Match_Date LIKE '2013%'

Question:
Provide the full names and emails of customers whose payments were greater than 70% of the average.

Evidence:
full name refers to first_name, last_name; average payment refers to AVG(amount); payments were greater than 70% of the average refers to amount > (AVG(amount) MULTIPLY 0.7)
answer: SELECT DISTINCT T2.first_name, T2.last_name, T2.email FROM payment AS T1 INNER JOIN customer AS T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id INNER JOIN address AS T3 ON T2.address_id = T3.address_id WHERE T1.amount > ( SELECT AVG(amount) FROM payment ) * 0.7

Question:
From 1960 to 1970, what is the total point of all-star players who are still alive?

answer: SELECT SUM(T2.points) FROM players AS T1 INNER JOIN player_allstar AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.season_id BETWEEN 1960 AND 1970 AND T1.deathDate = '0000-00-00'

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start with `game_platform`, which records each platform release and its year I join `platform` through the platform id so I can retrieve each platform's name I restrict the releases to the year 2000: `FROM game_platform AS T1 INNER JOIN platform AS T2 ON T1.platform_id = T2.id WHERE T1.release_year = 2000`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I select the platform names with DISTINCT so a platform appears only once across matching games This completes the query for the distinct names of platforms with games released in 2000: `SELECT DISTINCT T2.platform_name FROM game_platform AS T1 INNER JOIN platform AS T2 ON T1.platform_id = T2.id WHERE T1.release_year = 2000`.

Question:
State the employee who are born in or after 1970 and with the least sick leave hour.

Evidence:
born in or after 1970 refers to year(BirthDate) > = 1970;
answer: SELECT T2.FirstName, T2.LastName FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN Person AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.BirthDate) > '1970' ORDER BY T1.SickLeaveHours LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start with `Employee`, which contains birth dates and sick leave hours I join `Person` on the shared business entity id so I can retrieve each employee's name I keep employees whose extracted birth year is later than 1970: `FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN Person AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.BirthDate) > '1970'`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I sort the qualifying employees by sick leave hours and retain the one with the least Finally, I return that employee's first and last names: `SELECT T2.FirstName, T2.LastName FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN Person AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.BirthDate) > '1970' ORDER BY T1.SickLeaveHours LIMIT 1`.

Question:
List the maximum scores of the team Boston Red Stockings when the team won in postseason?
answer: SELECT max(T1.wins) FROM postseason AS T1 JOIN team AS T2 ON T1.team_id_winner  =  T2.team_id_br WHERE T2.name  =  'Boston Red Stockings';

Question:
What are the names of nations where both English and French are official languages?
answer: SELECT T1.Name FROM country AS T1 JOIN countrylanguage AS T2 ON T1.Code  =  T2.CountryCode WHERE T2.Language  =  "English" AND T2.IsOfficial  =  "T" INTERSECT SELECT T1.Name FROM country AS T1 JOIN countrylanguage AS T2 ON T1.Code  =  T2.CountryCode WHERE T2.Language  =  "French" AND T2.IsOfficial  =  "T"

Question:
What is the highest salary among each team? List the team name, id and maximum salary.
answer: SELECT T1.name ,  T1.team_id ,  max(T2.salary) FROM team AS T1 JOIN salary AS T2 ON T1.team_id  =  T2.team_id GROUP BY T1.team_id;

metadata.question: What is the highest salary among each team? List the team name, id and maximum salary.

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start with `team` to obtain each team's name and id I join `salary` on the team id so each team is associated with its salary records I group the matched records by team id so the salary aggregate is calculated for each team: `FROM team AS T1 JOIN salary AS T2 ON T1.team_id = T2.team_id GROUP BY T1.team_id`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I project the team name and id for each resulting group I add the maximum salary for each team group, completing the query: `SELECT T1.name ,  T1.team_id ,  max(T2.salary) FROM team AS T1 JOIN salary AS T2 ON T1.team_id  =  T2.team_id GROUP BY T1.team_id;`.

Question:
Of all the countries that share territory with more than one continent, in which of them does the average population not exceed 10 inhabitants per square kilometer?
answer: SELECT NAME FROM country WHERE CODE IN ( SELECT country FROM encompasses GROUP BY country HAVING COUNT(continent) > 1 ) AND population / Area <= 10

prefix_hints.hint_2: I then require population divided by area to be at most 10 inhabitants per square kilometer Finally, I return the names of the qualifying countries: `SELECT NAME FROM country WHERE CODE IN ( SELECT country FROM encompasses GROUP BY country HAVING COUNT(continent) > 1 ) AND population / Area <= 10`.

Question:
What is the average number of reckless homicides that happened in a district?

Evidence:
"RECKLESS HOMICIDE" is the secondary_description; average = Divide (Count(report_no), Count(district_name))
answer: SELECT CAST(COUNT(T2.report_no) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT T1.district_name) FROM District AS T1 INNER JOIN Crime AS T2 ON T2.district_no = T1.district_no INNER JOIN IUCR AS T3 ON T3.iucr_no = T2.iucr_no WHERE T3.secondary_description = 'RECKLESS HOMICIDE'

Aaron Mooy refers to player_name = 'Aaron Mooy'; on 2016/2/4 refers to date LIKE '2016-02-04%';

Question:
What is the total actual profit gained from orders made by American customers from 2003-01-06 to 2005-05-09?

Evidence:
total actual profit = SUM(SUBTRACT(priceEach, buyPrice)); American is a nationality of country = 'USA'; orderDate BETWEEN '2003-01-06' AND '2005-05-09';
answer: SELECT SUM(T2.priceEach - T1.buyPrice) FROM products AS T1 INNER JOIN orderdetails AS T2 ON T1.productCode = T2.productCode INNER JOIN orders AS T3 ON T2.orderNumber = T3.orderNumber INNER JOIN customers AS T4 ON T3.customerNumber = T4.customerNumber WHERE T3.orderDate > '2003-01-05' AND T3.orderDate < '2005-05-10'

Question:
Which claims caused more than 2 settlements or have the maximum claim value? List the date the claim was made and the claim id.
answer: SELECT T1.Date_Claim_Made ,  T1.Claim_id FROM Claims AS T1 JOIN Settlements AS T2 ON T1.Claim_id  =  T2.Claim_id GROUP BY T1.Claim_id HAVING count(*)  >  2 UNION SELECT T1.Date_Claim_Made ,  T1.Claim_id FROM Claims AS T1 JOIN Settlements AS T2 ON T1.Claim_id  =  T2.Claim_id WHERE T1.Amount_Claimed  =  ( SELECT max(Amount_Claimed) FROM Claims )

closing day refers to SUBTRACT(days.day_id, business_Hours.day_id)
answer: SELECT T3.day_id - T2.day_id FROM Business AS T1 INNER JOIN Business_Hours AS T2 ON T1.business_id = T2.business_id INNER JOIN Days AS T3 ON T2.day_id = T3.day_id WHERE T1.state = 'SC'

Question:
Among the active employees with over 10 hours of sick leave, what is the percentage of the employees with over 20 vacation hours?

Evidence:
CurrentFlag = 1 refers to the active status of employees; Percentage = Divide (Count (BusinessEntityID (CurrentFlag = 1 & VacationHours >20 & SickLeaveHours > 10)), Count (BusinessEntityID (CurrentFlag = 1 & SickLeaveHours>10))) * 100;
answer: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.VacationHours > 20 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.BusinessEntityID) FROM EmployeePayHistory AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T2.CurrentFlag = 1 AND T2.SickLeaveHours > 10

Question:
What is the percentage of the most common conditions for patients age 60 and above?

Evidence:
most common condition refers to MAX(COUNT(conditions.DESCRIPTION)); age 60 and above refers to SUBTRACT(conditions.START, birthdate) > 60; percentage = MULTIPLY(DIVIDE(SUM(patients.patient WHERE MAX(COUNT(conditions.DESCRIPTION)) AND SUBTRACT(conditions.START, birthdate) > 60))), COUNT(patients.patient WHERE MAX(COUNT(conditions.DESCRIPTION)), 10);

Question:
Calculate the percentage of the weight of goods being transported by Zachery Hicks to California in year 2016.

Evidence:
"California" is the state; in 2016 refers to CAST (ship_date AS DATE) = 2016; percentage = Divide (Sum(weight where first_name = 'Zachery' AND last_name = 'Hicks'), Sum(weight)) * 100
answer: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.first_name = 'Zachery' AND T2.last_name = 'Hicks' THEN T1.weight ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(T1.weight) FROM shipment AS T1 INNER JOIN driver AS T2 ON T1.driver_id = T2.driver_id WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.ship_date) = '2016'

Question:
Name all products that started selling in 2013. State its respective vendor's name.

Evidence:
Started selling in 2013 refers to year(SellStartDate) = 2013;
answer: SELECT T1.Name, T3.Name FROM Product AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductVendor AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID INNER JOIN Vendor AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.SellStartDate) = '2013'

metadata.question: Name all products that started selling in 2013. State its respective vendor's name.

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start with `Product` because it contains each product's name and selling start date I link each product to its vendor relationship through the shared product ID I then join `Vendor` on the business entity ID so the vendor name is available: `FROM Product AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductVendor AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID INNER JOIN Vendor AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I keep products whose selling start year is 2013 using SQLite's `STRFTIME` function Finally, I return each qualifying product name with its respective vendor name: `SELECT T1.Name, T3.Name FROM Product AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductVendor AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID INNER JOIN Vendor AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.SellStartDate) = '2013'`.

Question:
What is the name of department where has the largest number of professors with a Ph.D. degree?
answer: SELECT T2.dept_name ,  T1.dept_code FROM professor AS T1 JOIN department AS T2 ON T1.dept_code  =  T2.dept_code WHERE T1.prof_high_degree  =  'Ph.D.' GROUP BY T1.dept_code ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1

metadata.question: What is the name of department where has the largest number of professors with a Ph.D. degree?

prefix_hints.hint_1: Professor degree data and department names are in separate tables, so I join `professor` to `department` on the department code I keep the professors whose highest degree is a Ph.D. I group the matching professors by department so each department's rows can be counted: `FROM professor AS T1 JOIN department AS T2 ON T1.dept_code = T2.dept_code WHERE T1.prof_high_degree = 'Ph.D.' GROUP BY T1.dept_code`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I sort the department groups by professor count in descending order and retain the largest one Finally, I return that department's name and code: `SELECT T2.dept_name ,  T1.dept_code FROM professor AS T1 JOIN department AS T2 ON T1.dept_code  =  T2.dept_code WHERE T1.prof_high_degree  =  'Ph.D.' GROUP BY T1.dept_code ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
Find the first name, last name and id for the top three players won the most player awards.
answer: SELECT T1.name_first ,  T1.name_last ,  T1.player_id FROM player AS T1 JOIN player_award AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id GROUP BY T1.player_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 3;

metadata.question: Find the first name, last name and id for the top three players won the most player awards.

prefix_hints.hint_1: I link each player to their award records through the shared player id I group the joined award records by player so each player has one result group I order those player groups by their number of award records from highest to lowest: `FROM player AS T1 JOIN player_award AS T2 ON T1.player_id = T2.player_id GROUP BY T1.player_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I retain the first three groups to get the three players with the most awards I project each qualifying player's first name, last name, and id, completing the query: `SELECT T1.name_first ,  T1.name_last ,  T1.player_id FROM player AS T1 JOIN player_award AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id GROUP BY T1.player_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 3;`.

Question:
Please list the products that are out of stock and purchased in house.

Evidence:
take more than 2 days to make refers to DaysToManufacture>2; out of stock refers to OnOrderQty = 0 or OnOrderQty is null; manufactured in house refers to MakeFlag = 1
answer: SELECT T2.Name FROM ProductVendor AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.MakeFlag = 0 AND (T1.OnOrderQty IS NULL OR T1.OnOrderQty = 0)

Question:
List the brand names of bottled root beer whose first brewing year is no later than 1930.

Evidence:
bottled root beer refers to ContainerType = 'Bottle'; first brewing year is no later than 1930 refers to FirstBrewedYear < 1930;
answer: SELECT T2.BrandName FROM rootbeer AS T1 INNER JOIN rootbeerbrand AS T2 ON T1.BrandID = T2.BrandID WHERE T2.FirstBrewedYear < '1930-01-01' AND T1.ContainerType = 'Bottle' ORDER BY T2.FirstBrewedYear LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: The container type is recorded in `rootbeer`, while the brand details are in `rootbeerbrand`, so I join them by brand id I restrict the joined brands to those first brewed before the specified 1930 cutoff I then keep the root beer entries whose container type is Bottle: `FROM rootbeer AS T1 INNER JOIN rootbeerbrand AS T2 ON T1.BrandID = T2.BrandID WHERE T2.FirstBrewedYear < '1930-01-01' AND T1.ContainerType = 'Bottle'`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I sort the qualifying entries by first brewing year and retain the first one Finally, I return the brand name from that result: `SELECT T2.BrandName FROM rootbeer AS T1 INNER JOIN rootbeerbrand AS T2 ON T1.BrandID = T2.BrandID WHERE T2.FirstBrewedYear < '1930-01-01' AND T1.ContainerType = 'Bottle' ORDER BY T2.FirstBrewedYear LIMIT 1`.

Question:
What is the name of the sales person who handled the highest number of sales?

Evidence:
name of the sales person = FirstName, MiddleInitial, LastName; highest number of sales refers to MAX(COUNT(SalesID));
answer: SELECT T1.FirstName, T1.MiddleInitial, T1.LastName FROM Employees AS T1 INNER JOIN Sales AS T2 ON T2.SalesPersonID = T1.EmployeeID GROUP BY T2.SalesPersonID, T1.FirstName, T1.MiddleInitial, T1.LastName ORDER BY COUNT(T2.SalesID) DESC LIMIT 1

metadata.question: What is the name of the sales person who handled the highest number of sales?
metadata.evidence: name of the sales person = FirstName, MiddleInitial, LastName; highest number of sales refers to MAX(COUNT(SalesID));

prefix_hints.hint_1: I link each employee to the sales they handled using the salesperson foreign key I group the joined rows by salesperson and all three name fields so each employee's sales can be counted I order the employee groups by their sales counts in descending order, placing the highest count first: `FROM Employees AS T1 INNER JOIN Sales AS T2 ON T2.SalesPersonID = T1.EmployeeID GROUP BY T2.SalesPersonID, T1.FirstName, T1.MiddleInitial, T1.LastName ORDER BY COUNT(T2.SalesID) DESC`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I retain only the first group, which represents the salesperson who handled the most sales Finally, I project that salesperson's first name, middle initial, and last name: `SELECT T1.FirstName, T1.MiddleInitial, T1.LastName FROM Employees AS T1 INNER JOIN Sales AS T2 ON T2.SalesPersonID = T1.EmployeeID GROUP BY T2.SalesPersonID, T1.FirstName, T1.MiddleInitial, T1.LastName ORDER BY COUNT(T2.SalesID) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
Among the films starred by Reese West, what is the difference between the films that have store ID of 1 and store ID of 2?

Evidence:
result = subtract(count(film_id where store_id = 1), count(film_id where store_id = 2))
answer: SELECT SUM(IIF(T4.film_id = 1, 1, 0)) - SUM(IIF(T4.film_id = 2, 1, 0)) AS diff FROM film_actor AS T1 INNER JOIN actor AS T2 ON T1.actor_id = T2.actor_id INNER JOIN film AS T3 ON T1.film_id = T3.film_id INNER JOIN inventory AS T4 ON T3.film_id = T4.film_id WHERE T2.first_name = 'Reese' AND T2.last_name = 'West'

metadata.question: Among the films starred by Reese West, what is the difference between the films that have store ID of 1 and store ID of 2?

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start from the film-cast mapping and join the actor records so I can identify Reese West I join each cast entry to its film record I continue into inventory so the inventory film identifiers are available for the conditional counts: `FROM film_actor AS T1 INNER JOIN actor AS T2 ON T1.actor_id = T2.actor_id INNER JOIN film AS T3 ON T1.film_id = T3.film_id INNER JOIN inventory AS T4 ON T3.film_id = T4.film_id`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I restrict the joined rows to the actor whose first and last names are Reese West I conditionally count inventory rows whose film identifiers are 1 and 2, then subtract the second total from the first: `SELECT SUM(IIF(T4.film_id = 1, 1, 0)) - SUM(IIF(T4.film_id = 2, 1, 0)) AS diff FROM film_actor AS T1 INNER JOIN actor AS T2 ON T1.actor_id = T2.actor_id INNER JOIN film AS T3 ON T1.film_id = T3.film_id INNER JOIN inventory AS T4 ON T3.film_id = T4.film_id WHERE T2.first_name = 'Reese' AND T2.last_name = 'West'`.

Question:
List out the account numbers of female clients who are oldest and has lowest average salary, calculate the gap between this lowest average salary with the highest average salary?

Evidence:
Female means gender = 'F'; A11 refers to average salary; Gap = highest average salary - lowest average salary; If the person A's birthdate > B's birthdate, it means that person B is order than person A.
answer: SELECT T1.account_id , ( SELECT MAX(A11) - MIN(A11) FROM district ) FROM account AS T1 INNER JOIN district AS T2 ON T1.district_id = T2.district_id INNER JOIN disp AS T3 ON T1.account_id = T3.account_id INNER JOIN client AS T4 ON T3.client_id = T4.client_id WHERE T2.district_id = ( SELECT district_id FROM client WHERE gender = 'F' ORDER BY birth_date ASC LIMIT 1 ) ORDER BY T2.A11 DESC LIMIT 1

Question:
What is the average quantity of product that have been shipped by Federal Shipping in November 1996?

Evidence:
Federal Shipping refers to CompanyName = 'Federal Shipping'; DIVIDE(SUM(Quantity), COUNT(ProductID)) where CompanyName = 'Federal Shipping' and ShippedDate > = '1996-11-01 00:00:00' AND ShippedDate < '1996-12-01 00:00:00';
answer: SELECT CAST(SUM(T2.Quantity) AS REAL) / COUNT(T2.OrderID) FROM Orders AS T1 INNER JOIN `Order Details` AS T2 ON T1.OrderID = T2.OrderID INNER JOIN Shippers AS T3 ON T1.ShipVia = T3.ShipperID WHERE T1.ShippedDate LIKE '1996-11%' AND T3.CompanyName = 'Federal Shipping'

name of the customer refers to c_name; delivered the longest refers to max(subtract(l_receiptdate, l_commitdate))

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start from `player`, where each player's height is stored I connect each player to their college history through `player_college` I then join `college` so the institution's full name is available: `FROM player AS T1 JOIN player_college AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id JOIN college AS T3 ON T3.college_id  =  T2.college_id`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I restrict the joined records to Yale University I average the heights of those matched players, completing the query: `SELECT avg(T1.height) FROM player AS T1 JOIN player_college AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id JOIN college AS T3 ON T3.college_id  =  T2.college_id WHERE T3.name_full  =  'Yale University';`.

Question:
What is the total number of crimes that happened in Bridgeport with beat less than 1000?

Evidence:
Bridgeport refers to community_area_name = 'Bridgeport'; with beat less than 1000 refers to beat < 1000; total number = count(beat) where community_area_name = 'Bridgeport' and beat < 1000
answer: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T2.beat < 1000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM Community_Area AS T1 INNER JOIN Crime AS T2 ON T2.community_area_no = T1.community_area_no WHERE T1.community_area_name = 'Bridgeport'

Question:

Evidence:
Baltic Sea is a sea located in Northern Europe
answer: SELECT AVG(T1.Population) FROM city AS T1 INNER JOIN located AS T2 ON T1.Name = T2.City INNER JOIN sea AS T3 ON T3.Name = T2.Sea WHERE T3.Name = 'Baltic Sea'

prefix_hints.hint_2: I restrict the joined rows to the Baltic Sea Finally, I average the populations of those cities: `SELECT AVG(T1.Population) FROM city AS T1 INNER JOIN located AS T2 ON T1.Name = T2.City INNER JOIN sea AS T3 ON T3.Name = T2.Sea WHERE T3.Name = 'Baltic Sea'`.

Question:
What is the full name of the driver who delivered the most shipments to the least populated city?

Evidence:
least populated city refers to Min(population); fullname refers to first_name, last_name; most shipment refers to driver_id where Max(Count (ship_id))
answer: SELECT T1.first_name, T1.last_name FROM driver AS T1 INNER JOIN shipment AS T2 ON T1.driver_id = T2.driver_id INNER JOIN city AS T3 ON T3.city_id = T2.city_id GROUP BY T1.first_name, T1.last_name, T3.population HAVING T3.population = MAX(T3.population) ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

metadata.evidence: least populated city refers to Min(population); fullname refers to first_name, last_name; most shipment refers to driver_id where Max(Count (ship_id))

prefix_hints.hint_2: I retain the population group matching the aggregate population condition, rank drivers by shipment count descending, and keep the top one Finally, I project the selected driver's first and last names, completing the query: `SELECT T1.first_name, T1.last_name FROM driver AS T1 INNER JOIN shipment AS T2 ON T1.driver_id = T2.driver_id INNER JOIN city AS T3 ON T3.city_id = T2.city_id GROUP BY T1.first_name, T1.last_name, T3.population HAVING T3.population = MAX(T3.population) ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1`.

answer: SELECT t3.customer_details FROM claim_headers AS t1 JOIN policies AS t2 ON t1.policy_id  =  t2.policy_id JOIN customers AS t3 ON t2.customer_id  =  t3.customer_id WHERE t1.amount_piad  =  (SELECT min(amount_piad) FROM claim_headers)

metadata.question: Which customer made the smallest amount of claim in one claim? Return the customer details.

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start from the claim records because each individual claimed amount is stored in `amount_piad` I join each claim to its policy so I can identify the associated customer I continue from the policy to the customer record that contains the requested details: `FROM claim_headers AS t1 JOIN policies AS t2 ON t1.policy_id  =  t2.policy_id JOIN customers AS t3 ON t2.customer_id  =  t3.customer_id`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I keep the claim whose paid amount equals the minimum paid amount across all claim headers I return the details of the customer associated with that smallest claim amount: `SELECT t3.customer_details FROM claim_headers AS t1 JOIN policies AS t2 ON t1.policy_id  =  t2.policy_id JOIN customers AS t3 ON t2.customer_id  =  t3.customer_id WHERE t1.amount_piad  =  (SELECT min(amount_piad) FROM claim_headers)`.

Question:
Calculate the average number of shipments that Zachery Hicks shipped in year 2017.

Evidence:
in year 2017 refers to CAST(ship_date AS DATE) = 2017; percentage = Divide (Count(ship_id where first_name = 'Zachery' AND last_name = 'Hicks'), Count(ship_id)) * 100
answer: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.first_name = 'Zachery' AND T2.last_name = 'Hicks' THEN T1.ship_id ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(*) FROM shipment AS T1 INNER JOIN driver AS T2 ON T1.driver_id = T2.driver_id WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.ship_date) = '2017'

Question:
How many businesses with the category are open from Monday to Thursday?

Evidence:
open from Monday to Thursday refers to day_of_week BETWEEN Monday AND Thursday and day_id BETWEEN 2 AND 5;
answer: SELECT COUNT(T2.business_id) FROM Categories AS T1 INNER JOIN Business_Categories AS T2 ON T1.category_id = T2.category_id INNER JOIN Business AS T3 ON T2.business_id = T3.business_id INNER JOIN Business_Hours AS T4 ON T3.business_id = T4.business_id INNER JOIN Days AS T5 ON T4.day_id = T5.day_id WHERE T5.day_of_week LIKE 'Monday' OR T5.day_of_week LIKE 'Tuesday' OR T5.day_of_week LIKE 'Wednesday' OR T5.day_of_week LIKE 'Thursday'

Question:
On which continent is the country with the most erosion of real income?

Evidence:
highest inflation rate results in the most erosion of real income
answer: SELECT T1.Name FROM continent AS T1 INNER JOIN encompasses AS T2 ON T1.Name = T2.Continent INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T3.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN economy AS T4 ON T4.Country = T3.Code ORDER BY T4.Inflation DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_2: Since the highest inflation represents the most erosion of real income, I sort inflation descending and retain the top row I project the name of the continent associated with that country, completing the query: `SELECT T1.Name FROM continent AS T1 INNER JOIN encompasses AS T2 ON T1.Name = T2.Continent INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T3.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN economy AS T4 ON T4.Country = T3.Code ORDER BY T4.Inflation DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
Among the professors with more than average teaching ability, list the full name and email address of the professors who advise two or more students.

Evidence:
more than average teaching ability refers to teachingability > AVG(teachingability); full_name of the professor = first_name, last_name; email address of the professor refers to email; advises two or more students refers to COUNT(student_id) > = 2;
answer: SELECT T2.first_name, T2.last_name, T2.email FROM RA AS T1 INNER JOIN prof AS T2 ON T1.prof_id = T2.prof_id WHERE T2.teachingability > ( SELECT AVG(teachingability) FROM prof ) GROUP BY T2.prof_id HAVING COUNT(T1.student_id) >= 2

Question:
How many business are opened for more than 8 hour in Mesa and what is the percentage of the active businesses?

Evidence:
business are opened for more than 8 hours refer to business_id where SUBTRACT(closing_time, opening_time) > 8; DIVIDE(COUNT(business_id where active = 'true' and city = 'Mesa' and SUBTRACT(closing_time, opening_time) > 8), COUNT(business_id where city = 'Mesa' and SUBTRACT(closing_time, opening_time) > 8)) as percentage;
answer: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.active = 'true' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.business_id) AS ACT FROM Business AS T1 INNER JOIN Business_Hours AS T2 ON T1.business_id = T2.business_id WHERE T1.city = 'Mesa'

Question:
List the purchase order whereby all received quantity were rejected? Name those product.

Evidence:
Rejected refers rejected product in which to RejectedQty = 1
answer: SELECT T1.Name FROM Product AS T1 INNER JOIN PurchaseOrderDetail AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.RejectedQty = T2.ReceivedQty AND T2.RejectedQty <> 0

metadata.question: List the purchase order whereby all received quantity were rejected? Name those product.
metadata.evidence: Rejected refers rejected product in which to RejectedQty = 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start with `Product` so I can return the names of the products I join each product to its purchase order details through `ProductID`, where the received and rejected quantities are recorded I keep purchase order lines where the rejected quantity equals the entire received quantity: `FROM Product AS T1 INNER JOIN PurchaseOrderDetail AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.RejectedQty = T2.ReceivedQty`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I also require a nonzero rejected quantity so that zero-receipt lines are excluded Finally, I project the names of the products on those fully rejected purchase order lines: `SELECT T1.Name FROM Product AS T1 INNER JOIN PurchaseOrderDetail AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.RejectedQty = T2.ReceivedQty AND T2.RejectedQty <> 0`.

Question:
In what percentage of games played at the Dr DY Patil Sports Academy venue did the winning team win by a margin of less than 10?

Evidence:
Dr DY Patil Sports Academy venue refers to Venue_Name = 'Dr DY Patil Sports Academy'; win by a margin of less than 10 refers to Win_Margin < 10; percentage = divide(count(Venue_Id) when Win_Margin < 10, sum(Venue_Id)) as percentage
answer: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.Win_Margin < 10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / TOTAL(T1.Venue_Id) FROM Venue AS T1 INNER JOIN Match AS T2 ON T1.Venue_Id = T2.Venue_Id WHERE T1.Venue_Name = 'Dr DY Patil Sports Academy'

Question:
Give the full name of the actor who acted in the most number of movies?

Evidence:
full name refers to first_name, last_name; acted in the most number of movies refers to MAX(COUNT(film_id))
answer: SELECT T.first_name, T.last_name FROM ( SELECT T2.first_name, T2.last_name, COUNT(T1.film_id) AS num FROM film_actor AS T1 INNER JOIN actor AS T2 ON T1.actor_id = T2.actor_id GROUP BY T2.first_name, T2.last_name ) AS T ORDER BY T.num DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start with `playstore`, where each app's price is stored I join the reviews by app name so each app is associated with its sentiment polarity values I identify the highest listed price with a scalar subquery over `playstore`: `SELECT MAX(Price) FROM playstore`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I restrict the joined rows to the app whose price equals that maximum Finally, I sum the sentiment polarity values for the reviews of that most expensive app: `SELECT SUM(T2.Sentiment_Polarity) FROM playstore AS T1 INNER JOIN user_reviews AS T2 ON T1.App = T2.App WHERE T1.Price = ( SELECT MAX(Price) FROM playstore )`.

metadata.question: Indicate, by region, which platform has sold the most games.
metadata.evidence: region refers to region_name; platform refers to game_platform; sold the most games refers to MAX(SUM(num_sales));

prefix_hints.hint_1: I connect each platform to its game-platform records, regional sales, and region name through the specified keys I group the joined sales records by platform and region so the sales can be totaled for each combination I rank those groups by total sales in descending order and retain the highest-selling one: `FROM platform AS T1 INNER JOIN game_platform AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.platform_id INNER JOIN region_sales AS T3 ON T1.id = T3.game_platform_id INNER JOIN region AS T4 ON T3.region_id = T4.id GROUP BY T1.platform_name, T4.region_name ORDER BY SUM(T3.num_sales) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
For each customer who has at least two orders, find the customer name and number of orders made.
answer: SELECT T2.customer_name ,  count(*) FROM orders AS T1 JOIN customers AS T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id GROUP BY T2.customer_id HAVING count(*)  >=  2

intermediate_turns.sql: SELECT * ,  count ( * )  FROM orders AS T1 JOIN customers AS T2 ON T1.customer_id  =  T2.customer_id GROUP BY T2.customer_id HAVING count ( * )    > =    2

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start from the orders and join each one to its customer through the shared customer id I group the joined rows by customer so each group represents all orders made by one customer I retain customer groups containing at least two orders: `FROM orders AS T1 JOIN customers AS T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id GROUP BY T2.customer_id HAVING count(*) >= 2`.

Question:
Among the crimes located in the community area with the highest population, what is the percentage of domestic violence?

Evidence:
the highest population refers to max(population); domestic violence refers to domestic = 'TRUE'; percentage = divide(count(domestic = 'TRUE'), count(domestic)) where population = max(population) * 100%
answer: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.domestic = 'TRUE' THEN T2.domestic END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T2.domestic) FROM Community_Area AS T1 INNER JOIN Crime AS T2 ON T2.community_area_no = T1.community_area_no GROUP BY T1.community_area_no HAVING COUNT(T1.population) ORDER BY COUNT(T1.population) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: I link each community area to its crimes through the shared community area number I group the joined crimes by community area so the domestic percentage and population-based ranking are calculated per area I retain grouped community areas with a population count through the HAVING expression: `FROM Community_Area AS T1 INNER JOIN Crime AS T2 ON T2.community_area_no = T1.community_area_no GROUP BY T1.community_area_no HAVING COUNT(T1.population)`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I rank those groups by the population count in descending order and keep the first one I count domestic crimes conditionally, cast that count to REAL, and divide it by the count of non-null domestic values before multiplying by 100: `SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.domestic = 'TRUE' THEN T2.domestic END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T2.domestic) FROM Community_Area AS T1 INNER JOIN Crime AS T2 ON T2.community_area_no = T1.community_area_no GROUP BY T1.community_area_no HAVING COUNT(T1.population) ORDER BY COUNT(T1.population) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
Among the coaches who have served more than 2 NBA teams, during which coach's period of coaching, a team has the least numbers of games lost in the post-season games?

Evidence:
served more than 2 NBA teams refers to count (tmID) > = 2; least number of game lost in post season refers to Min(post_losses)

Question:
Among the salable products from the mountain product line, how many of them have the most reviews?

Evidence:
salable product refers to FinishedGoodsFlag = 1; mountain product line refers to ProductLine = 'M'
answer: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T2.ProductLine = 'M' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.FinishedGoodsFlag = 1 GROUP BY T1.ProductID ORDER BY COUNT(T1.ProductReviewID) DESC LIMIT 1

metadata.evidence: salable product refers to FinishedGoodsFlag = 1; mountain product line refers to ProductLine = 'M'

prefix_hints.hint_1: I connect each review to its product so the review counts and product attributes are available together I restrict the joined rows to salable products using the finished-goods flag I group the remaining reviews by product so each group represents the reviews received by one salable product: `FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.FinishedGoodsFlag = 1 GROUP BY T1.ProductID`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I rank those product groups by review count in descending order and retain the product with the most reviews For that top-reviewed group, I sum one for each review whose product belongs to the mountain product line: `SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T2.ProductLine = 'M' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.FinishedGoodsFlag = 1 GROUP BY T1.ProductID ORDER BY COUNT(T1.ProductReviewID) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
List all goalies from year 2000 to 2010 for team COL. State their given name, height, weight and age of today.

Evidence:
team COL refers to tmID = 'COL'; age of today refers to SUBTRACT(YEAR(NOW())-birthYear)
answer: SELECT T1.nameGiven, T1.height , T1.weight, STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - birthYear FROM Master AS T1 INNER JOIN Goalies AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.tmID = 'COL' AND T2.year >= 2000 AND T2.year <= 2010 GROUP BY T1.playerID

prefix_hints.hint_1: I link each goalie record to the corresponding player details through `playerID` I restrict the joined records to goalies who played for team COL I narrow the seasons to the inclusive range from 2000 through 2010: `FROM Master AS T1 INNER JOIN Goalies AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.tmID = 'COL' AND T2.year >= 2000 AND T2.year <= 2010`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: A goalie may have records for multiple seasons, so I group by player to return one row per goalie I project each goalie's given name, height, weight, and current age calculated as the current year minus birth year: `SELECT T1.nameGiven, T1.height , T1.weight, STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - birthYear FROM Master AS T1 INNER JOIN Goalies AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.tmID = 'COL' AND T2.year >= 2000 AND T2.year <= 2010 GROUP BY T1.playerID`.

DIVIDE(SUM(total_beneficiaries), COUNT(zip_code)) where name = 'Guam';

"Hotel & Travel" is the category_name; most review refers to Max(Count(category_id)); Average star per user = Divide (Sum (review_stars), Count(user_id))

How many organizations are established in the country with the most ethnic groups?
answer: SELECT COUNT(T2.Province) FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN organization AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T3 ON T3.Country = T2.Country GROUP BY T1.Name ORDER BY COUNT(T3.Name) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start by linking each country to its established organizations through the country code I then join the ethnic groups recorded for each organization’s country I group the joined rows by country name so the organization and ethnic-group counts are calculated country by country: `FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN organization AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T3 ON T3.Country = T2.Country GROUP BY T1.Name`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I rank the country groups by their ethnic-group row count in descending order and retain the top one Finally, I return the count of organization province values for that top-ranked country: `SELECT COUNT(T2.Province) FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN organization AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T3 ON T3.Country = T2.Country GROUP BY T1.Name ORDER BY COUNT(T3.Name) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
Among the movies released from 1991 to 2000, calculate the percentage of comedy movies. Provide any five movie titles and directors.

Evidence:
DIVIDE(COUNT(movie_title where genre = 'Comedy'), COUNT(movie_title)) as percentage where substr(release_date, length(release_date) - 3, length(release_date)) between '1991' and '2000';
answer: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T1.genre = 'Comedy' THEN T1.movie_title ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.movie_title), group_concat(T1.movie_title), group_concat(T2.director) FROM movies_total_gross AS T1 INNER JOIN director AS T2 ON T1.movie_title = T2.name WHERE SUBSTR(T1.release_date, LENGTH(T1.release_date) - 3, LENGTH(T1.release_date)) BETWEEN '1991' AND '2000'

Question:
List the name and calculate its profit for product with the highest rating in review.

Evidence:
Profit = SUBTRACT(ListPrice, StandardCost); the highest rating in review refers to Rating = 5
answer: SELECT T1.Name, T1.ListPrice - T1.StandardCost FROM Product AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductReview AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID ORDER BY T2.Rating DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_2: I restrict the subtracted set to customers whose invoice total exceeds 20 This set difference now returns the last names of customers without invoice totals exceeding 20: `SELECT LastName FROM CUSTOMER EXCEPT SELECT T1.LastName FROM CUSTOMER AS T1 JOIN Invoice AS T2 ON T1.CustomerId  =  T2.CustomerId WHERE T2.total  >  20`.

prefix_hints.hint_2: For the alternative condition, I union those results with companies joined to their maintenance contracts I group the second branch by company and retain those with at least two contracts, completing both sides of the condition: `SELECT T1.company_id ,  T1.company_name FROM Third_Party_Companies AS T1 JOIN Maintenance_Engineers AS T2 ON T1.company_id  =  T2.company_id GROUP BY T1.company_id HAVING count(*)  >=  2 UNION SELECT T3.company_id ,  T3.company_name FROM Third_Party_Companies AS T3 JOIN Maintenance_Contracts AS T4 ON T3.company_id  =  T4.maintenance_contract_company_id GROUP BY T3.company_id HAVING count(*)  >=  2`.

Question:
Which year recorded the most consumption of gas paid in CZK?

Evidence:
The first 4 strings of the Date values in the yearmonth table can represent year.
answer: SELECT SUBSTR(T2.Date, 1, 4) FROM customers AS T1 INNER JOIN yearmonth AS T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID WHERE T1.Currency = 'CZK' GROUP BY SUBSTR(T2.Date, 1, 4) ORDER BY SUM(T2.Consumption) DESC LIMIT 1

colour refers to ATT_CLASS; van refers to OBJ_CLASS = 'van'; image no. 1 refers to IMG_ID = 1
answer: SELECT T4.ATT_CLASS FROM IMG_OBJ AS T1 INNER JOIN OBJ_CLASSES AS T2 ON T1.OBJ_CLASS_ID = T2.OBJ_CLASS_ID INNER JOIN IMG_OBJ_ATT AS T3 ON T1.IMG_ID = T3.IMG_ID INNER JOIN ATT_CLASSES AS T4 ON T3.ATT_CLASS_ID = T4.ATT_CLASS_ID WHERE T2.OBJ_CLASS = 'van' AND T1.IMG_ID = 1 GROUP BY T4.ATT_CLASS

Question:
What's the number of infant mortality in Switzerland in a year?

Evidence:
Number can be calculated = Infant_Mortality * Population * Population_Growth
answer: SELECT T2.Infant_Mortality * T1.Population * T2.Population_Growth FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN population AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T1.Name = 'Switzerland'

Question:
What is the name of the aircraft that has won an award the most?
answer: SELECT T1.Aircraft FROM aircraft AS T1 JOIN MATCH AS T2 ON T1.Aircraft_ID  =  T2.Winning_Aircraft GROUP BY T2.Winning_Aircraft ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start with the aircraft table and select the aircraft name I join each aircraft to its winning matches using the aircraft identifier I group the matches by winning aircraft so each aircraft's wins can be counted: `SELECT T1.Aircraft FROM aircraft AS T1 JOIN MATCH AS T2 ON T1.Aircraft_ID  =  T2.Winning_Aircraft GROUP BY T2.Winning_Aircraft`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I order the aircraft groups by their match counts in descending order, placing the aircraft with the most wins first I keep only the first result to return the aircraft with the most wins: `SELECT T1.Aircraft FROM aircraft AS T1 JOIN MATCH AS T2 ON T1.Aircraft_ID  =  T2.Winning_Aircraft GROUP BY T2.Winning_Aircraft ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:

Evidence:
'Agent Truman' is a title of a film; category refers to name
answer: SELECT T3.name FROM film AS T1 INNER JOIN film_category AS T2 ON T1.film_id = T2.film_id INNER JOIN category AS T3 ON T2.category_id = T3.category_id WHERE T1.title = 'AGENT TRUMAN'

Question:

Question:
For all the Yelp businesses that allow customers bring their own beer, what percentage of them are in "Phoenix"?

Evidence:
bring their own beer refers to attribute_name = 'BYOB' AND attribute_value = 'TRUE'; Phoenix refers to city = 'Phoenix'; percentage = MULTIPLY(DIVIDE(SUM(city = 'Phoenix'), COUNT(business_id)), 1.0)
answer: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T3.city LIKE 'Phoenix' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T2.business_id) AS "percentage" FROM Attributes AS T1 INNER JOIN Business_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.attribute_id = T2.attribute_id INNER JOIN Business AS T3 ON T2.business_id = T3.business_id WHERE T1.attribute_name LIKE 'BYOB' AND T2.attribute_value LIKE 'TRUE'

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start with the customer records that contain each customer's market segment and nation key I join each customer to their nation so I can identify customers in Germany I restrict the joined records to customers in the household market segment: `FROM customer AS T1 INNER JOIN nation AS T2 ON T1.c_nationkey = T2.n_nationkey WHERE T1.c_mktsegment = 'HOUSEHOLD'`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I further restrict those customers to the nation named Germany I count the customer names in the resulting set to return the requested number: `SELECT COUNT(T1.c_name) FROM customer AS T1 INNER JOIN nation AS T2 ON T1.c_nationkey = T2.n_nationkey WHERE T1.c_mktsegment = 'HOUSEHOLD' AND T2.n_name = 'GERMANY'`.

Question:
List all countries with negative growth in population. State the country, population and growth.

Evidence:
Negative growth in population means population_growth < 0
answer: SELECT T1.Name, T1.Population, T2.Population_Growth FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN population AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T2.Population_Growth < 0

Question:
Which authors have submitted to more than one workshop?
answer: SELECT T2.Author FROM acceptance AS T1 JOIN submission AS T2 ON T1.Submission_ID  =  T2.Submission_ID GROUP BY T2.Author HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT T1.workshop_id)  >  1

metadata.question: Which authors have submitted to more than one workshop?

prefix_hints.hint_1: I start from `acceptance`, where each accepted submission is associated with a workshop I join `submission` on the submission id so each workshop entry is connected to its author I group the joined records by author to evaluate workshop participation for each author: `FROM acceptance AS T1 JOIN submission AS T2 ON T1.Submission_ID  =  T2.Submission_ID GROUP BY T2.Author`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: I retain authors associated with more than one distinct workshop Finally, I return the qualifying author names: `SELECT T2.Author FROM acceptance AS T1 JOIN submission AS T2 ON T1.Submission_ID  =  T2.Submission_ID GROUP BY T2.Author HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT T1.workshop_id)  >  1`.

What is the id, forname and surname of the driver who had the first position in terms of laptime at least twice?
answer: SELECT T1.driverid ,  T1.forename ,  T1.surname FROM drivers AS T1 JOIN laptimes AS T2 ON T1.driverid = T2.driverid WHERE POSITION  =  '1' GROUP BY T1.driverid HAVING count(*)  >=  2

Question:
What are the name and id of the team offering the lowest average salary?
answer: SELECT T1.name ,  T1.team_id FROM team AS T1 JOIN salary AS T2 ON T1.team_id = T2.team_id GROUP BY T1.team_id ORDER BY avg(T2.salary) ASC LIMIT 1;
